Houston's heavy-trash program has a twist that catches nearly everyone once: the city alternates what it collects each month, and **furniture only rides in even-numbered months.** Set a couch out in March and it's not early — it's illegal dumping, because March is a Tree Waste month and the trucks that come aren't allowed to take it.

## The Odd/Even System, Exactly

- **Junk Waste months — February, April, June, August, October, December:** furniture, appliances, and bulky household items are collected curbside on your neighborhood's scheduled heavy-trash day.
- **Tree Waste months — January, March, May, July, September, November:** clean wood waste only (limbs, branches, stumps). Furniture is explicitly not accepted; the separation is what lets the city mulch the tree waste.
- **Set-out rules:** at the curb after 6 PM the evening before your scheduled day, capped at **eight cubic yards** (roughly two pickup-truck loads) — oversized piles get skipped entirely.
- Find your neighborhood's heavy-trash day through the Solid Waste Department's schedule tools or the HTX Collects app; off-schedule set-outs are citable.

The practical catch: a couch that misses April's pickup waits until June. That's the longest potential gap of any major-city program in this series, and it's why Houston garages collect furniture.

## The Year-Round Alternative: Neighborhood Depositories

Houston runs **six Neighborhood Depository & Recycling Centers** that accept furniture any month — up to four visits per month per household, with a **limit of two large items like couches per visit**, proof of Houston residency required (utility bill or lease), vehicles two tons or under. If you have a truck and a free hour, this beats waiting for an even month.

**When neither fits** — odd month, no truck, or the couch is upstairs: [couch removal in Houston](/tx/houston/couch-removal/) starts at $90 any month of the year, carry-out included, [same-day in most ZIPs before 2PM EST](/book-online/). And a couch in good shape should skip the landfill math entirely — [donation pickup](/tx/houston/donation-pickup/) routes it to charity partners if it [passes condition standards](/blog/eco-friendly-living/can-couch-be-donated/). Pricing by item is in the [cost guide](/blog/junk-removal/how-much-does-couch-removal-cost/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What months does Houston pick up furniture?

Even-numbered months only — February, April, June, August, October, and December — on your neighborhood's scheduled Junk Waste day. Odd months are Tree Waste only, and furniture set out then is a violation, not an early start.

### How much junk waste can I set out in Houston?

Up to eight cubic yards per collection — about two pickup-truck beds. Piles over the cap don't get a partial pickup; they get left.

### Can I take a couch to a Houston dump myself?

Yes — the six Neighborhood Depositories accept furniture year-round from Houston residents: up to four visits a month, two large items like couches per visit, residency proof required.

### What if I can't wait for a Junk Waste month?

Booked removal runs every month: [same-day across most of Houston](/tx/houston/couch-removal/) before the 2PM EST cutoff, with the carry from inside your home included — no odd/even calendar involved.
